Otherwise, when noteClaimProject refuses, have the losing attempt void the project it just made through delivery's contract.

The round-2 finding asked for a race test with a create stub slower than CLAIM_SECONDS. None was added, so the stillClaimed guard and noteClaimProject's token check have no test. The resume test also leaves out two cases: the link failing after a real create inside promoteToDelivery, and a crash between create and noteClaimProject. Add table rows that run two promoteToDelivery calls with a slow or blocking create stub and claimed_at aged in between. Assert that no orphaned project is left, or that it gets voided. Also add a row whose recordPromotion really fails and then resumes.

The opportunity_project test plants the state with raw `update` SQL instead of driving promoteToDelivery or recordPromotion, and the finding asked for the resumed-claim path, which it does not cover. Both rows expect two rejections against HRI, so the test only shows that an existing holder blocks later links. It never races two new links where exactly one should win. Fix: run two promotions (sequential, concurrent, and through a resumed claim) whose create stubs return the same project id. Expect exactly one fulfilled and one rejected, and check that the test fails once the index is dropped.

Removing claim_project_id fixes the named orphan case by binding every stale claim to its key for good. That drops the variant the old code and the old test handled: a stale claim under which nothing was ever made can no longer move to another key. The claim is released only from promoteToDelivery's catch, and that release is best-effort (`.catch(logError)`). So a crash, timeout or failed release between claimPromotion and the create leaves the opportunity locked to that key, and the only way out is to create a project under it. Fix: when a stale claim's key differs, allow the takeover if `lookupKey(createKey(o.id, o.claim_key))` shows nothing was started or made under it. Do this inside the claim transaction, or have the idempotency record mark in-flight work, so the slow-create race does not come back.

The release decision is a check followed by a separate write. lookupKey reads in its own transaction, then releasePromotion runs, and nothing ties 'nothing was made' to the moment of release. If lookupKey reports a key, the claim is kept for good, even when the failure came after the create and will repeat on every replay. Examples: recordPromotion hits the opportunity_project unique index, or the client lookup fails. Every same-key retry replays the same project id and fails the same way, and every other key is refused, so the opportunity can never be promoted and nothing records it as stuck. Fix: if recordPromotion refuses a replayed project for a lasting reason, release the claim and flag the project, for example by voiding it through delivery's contract. Also make the release depend on the idempotency record inside the same transaction.

The previous finding asked for three variants of the shared-project race: sequential, concurrent, and through a resumed claim. Only the first two are here, so the resumed-claim row is missing. The test also checks only that one promotion wins. It never asserts what happens to the loser afterwards: whether its claim is released or the project flagged, and whether it can still be promoted. Add the resumed-claim row, and assert the loser's state after the race.

The release path changed from 'no project object' to 'lookupKey finds nothing'. The only release test fails before the create is ever called: delivery already has CON, so the pre-check throws. No row covers a create that delivery itself refuses or that throws, which is the case where withIdempotency has run. So nothing shows the claim is given back there, or that a different key works afterwards. The old row 'a stale claim that made nothing gives way to another key' was deleted and not replaced. Add table rows where the create stub throws (validation, forbidden, thrown before commit), each followed by a promote with another key that must succeed.

The fix for the slow-create race now depends on withIdempotency handling two creates that run at the same time under the same createKey. No test exercises that case. The 'slow first attempt' test holds attempt A at the gate before create is ever called. So A's create only starts after B has already created and linked the project, and A just gets a sequential replay. The test would stay green if withIdempotency had no handling for a create already in flight: no reservation, no lock, no unique key. Fix: block the stub inside delivery's create (after the insert, before the commit), or hold a DB lock, so both creates are in flight together. Then assert that exactly one project exists and that both attempts end with the opportunity linked to it.

createKey identifies a promotion by opportunity and key only. A retry that resumes the claim with different inputs gets back the project from the first attempt, with that attempt's billing, name and client. The new input is silently ignored and the promotion reports success. Fix: either include a fingerprint of the create input in the idempotency record and refuse a replay whose input differs, or refuse a resume whose billing differs from what the claim recorded.
